criteria.criterion: studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json has glossary entries (the array with 'in scope' and 'ship') for 'wake', 'endpoint', 'captain call', 'heartbeat' and 'durable record'. Each has a non-empty claims array of ids present in claims.json, or states in its definition that the firstmate source does not define the term, as the 'in scope' entry does. Checked by Grep and reading the diff.
criteria.evidence: intro.json lines 106-110 add all five entries to the glossary array. Each one opens with 'The firstmate source does not define ...' and cites existing claims: wake [c17], endpoint [c2,c3,c17], captain call [c23,c24], heartbeat [c9], durable record [c19]. I found each of these ids with Grep in claims.json.

criteria.criterion: The 'ship' entry's definition begins with a sentence saying a ship is a task that changes a project. It no longer opens with 'A kind of task, named next to scouts', and it keeps only claims c10, c12 and c18 or other existing claim ids. Checked in the diff of intro.json.
criteria.evidence: Line 105 now opens 'A task that changes a project: its work is delivered as a PR or, for a local-only ship, landed into the main local checkout, where a scout instead produces a report.' The old opening is gone. It cites c10, c12, c18, c37 and c39, and all five exist in claims.json.

criteria.criterion: Every new or reworded definition makes only statements found in the cited claims' text in claims.json. For example, a wake is described only through c17's stale wake, a heartbeat only through c9, an endpoint through c2, c3 and c17, a durable record through c19, and a captain call through c23 and c24. Where the claims do not say what a term is, the entry says so. A verifier can compare each definition with the cited claim text.
criteria.evidence: I compared each entry with the claim text. endpoint: c2 says refused 'before an endpoint ... exists', c3 says a deferred spawn exits 'before it ... creates an endpoint', and c17 says the agent 'inspects the recorded endpoint'. heartbeat: c9 'after every teardown and heartbeat'. durable record: c19 matches word for word. captain call: c23 matches. wake: c17's stale wake, plus 'endpoint of a worker', which is a light paraphrase of c17. In ship, 'landed into the main local checkout' comes from c37 and 'a scout instead produces a report' from c39. 'Delivered as a PR' is only implied by c37 ('A local-only ship has no PR'); c33's 'PR-based ship' would support it directly but is not cited (minor). The opening 'A task that changes a project' is the user's own required wording.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`. It succeeds, and the rendered index.html has a `<dt id="term-...">` glossary entry for each of the five terms. Each entry carries a `<span class="cites">` or says the source does not define the term. The 'ship' entry's first sentence says what a ship does.
criteria.evidence: The site command succeeded and wrote index.html under the target dir. Policy blocked me from reading that file, because it is outside the working dir. build() calls render(&load(STUDY_DIR)) (site.rs:639), and the tests render the same thing. the_real_cards_use_no_term_that_the_glossary_leaves_undefined passed: it asserts a <dt id="term-..."> for each of the five terms. the_ship_entry_opens_by_saying_what_a_ship_is (run inside 'glossary'? no, it ran in the full CI suite) asserts that '<dd>A task that changes a project' follows the ship entry. The render code emits <span class="cites"> for every non-page entry (site.rs:160, 473-478), and each new entry also says the source does not define the term.

criteria.criterion: A new test, in the unit tests in xtask/src/site.rs or in xtask/tests/site_page.rs, scans the rendered transition cards of the real study for each of the five terms. It fails when a term appears in a card and the glossary has no entry for it. Show that it fails: `cargo test -p xtask` with the test's own fixture where one entry is missing must produce the failure, or the test must assert on a fixture study that lacks one entry. It passes on the real study.
criteria.evidence: In a fixture study whose card uses 'Heartbeat' and 'durable record' with no glossary entries, card_terms_without_a_glossary_entry returns [heartbeat, durable record]; the fixture test asserts this and passed. The real-study test asserts that the helper returns an empty list there, and it passed. Taking out one of the new glossary entries would make that assertion, and the per-term loop, fail.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass. The existing site tests still pass, including the glossary alphabetical-order test, the in-scope test and the unknown-claim-citation test. No change is made to page structure or render code beyond what the new test needs.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded CI run 42650065203 for 6394364 shows fmt, clippy and test all passed. In my targeted run, all 6 xtask unit tests matching 'glossary' passed (including the alphabetical-order and in-scope tests), plus 1 site_page integration test. The diff to site.rs touches only the #[cfg(test)] mod tests; render code is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, Cargo configuration) are changed, and CHANGELOG.md is not edited unless the repository's habit requires it. Checked with `git diff --stat`.
criteria.evidence: Only intro.json and xtask/src/site.rs changed, so no governance file was touched. But the repository's habit does require a changelog entry for this kind of change. CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] records earlier glossary edits to this same study (line 3099: 'the Glossary gains green, red and home'; line 3438: 'Glossary: `exit 1` is added ... `ship` now says ...'). CHANGELOG.md is also listed as an expected deliverable, and the changelog default applies. The candidate adds no entry.

findings.summary: No CHANGELOG.md entry, although the changelog default applies, the expected deliverables list it, and the repository's habit is to record glossary changes to this study.
findings.evidence: git diff HEAD~1 --stat shows only intro.json and xtask/src/site.rs. CHANGELOG.md lines 3099-3104 and 3438-3442 record earlier glossary changes to the firstmate page. The brief's 'changelog' default says 'the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md'. The brief contradicts itself: its out-of-scope list names CHANGELOG.md, but criterion 7 allows the edit when the habit requires it, and here the habit does.

findings.summary: In the ship entry, 'its work is delivered as a PR' is only implied by the cited claims; the claim that states it is not cited.
findings.evidence: c37 says 'A local-only ship has no PR'. That implies other ships make PRs but does not say so. c33 ('a PR-based ship frees its place when its ready PR is recorded') states it more directly and is not in the entry's claims.

findings.summary: The card-term check matches plain substrings, so it can fire on longer words that contain a term (for example 'awake' contains 'wake').
findings.evidence: It uses `cards.contains(t)` on lowercased HTML. With five fixed terms and current data there are no false hits. A word-boundary match would be more exact.

findings.summary: The ship test checks that the text follows somewhere after the ship <dt>, not that the <dd> starts with it.
findings.evidence: It uses `html[at..].contains("<dd>A task that changes a project")`. A starts_with on the slice that begins at the <dd> would pin it to the ship entry.

summary: The content change does what was asked. The five glossary entries (wake, endpoint, captain call, heartbeat, durable record) each say the firstmate source does not define the term, and each cites only existing claims whose text supports what the entry says. The 'ship' entry now opens 'A task that changes a project'. Two new unit tests cover the check: one asserts that the real study's transition cards use none of the five terms without a glossary entry, and a fixture test shows the check finding the missing entries. These tests, the site build and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test results all pass. However, the candidate adds no CHANGELOG.md entry. The changelog default applies, CHANGELOG.md is an expected deliverable, and the repository records earlier glossary changes to this same page in [Unreleased]. That omission is a major finding, so the verdict is fail. Smaller points: the ship entry does not cite c33, which most directly supports 'delivered as a PR', and the term check matches plain substrings. I could not open the built index.html because it is outside the working directory; the rendered-page checks rest on unit tests that call the same render() the site command uses.
